title: You thought God forgot you.
paragraphs: You thought God forgot you.
Be honest.

Because if this is “purpose”… why does it feel like pressure?
If this is “calling”… why does it look like breaking?
If this is “grace”… why are you still in process?

That tension you feel?
That’s where most people quit.
But here’s the truth we don’t like to post:
God builds in silence before He reveals in public.
“For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand, that we should walk in them.” — Ephesians 2:10
Workmanship.

Not randomness.
Not wasted years.
Not emotional leftovers.

Workmanship means intention.
Design.
Hands-on formation.

And right now?
You’re in the hands.
Let me say something that might hit deep:
You are not stuck.
You are being shaped.

That delay you’re frustrated with?
It’s not punishment.

That closed door you cried over?
It’s not rejection.

That hidden season nobody sees?
It’s not meaningless.
It’s construction.
“And I am sure of this, that He who began a good work in you will bring it to completion at the day of Jesus Christ.” — Philippians 1:6
God does not abandon what He starts.
But here’s the part we struggle with…

We want the finished version of us
without surrendering to the forming version of us.

We want to preach,
but not be purified.

We want influence,
but not integrity.

We want elevation,
but not excavation.

And God says:
I love you too much to skip the process.
Look at the cross.

Jesus didn’t just die to give you a future.
He died to give you a new identity.
“Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come.” — 2 Corinthians 5:17
So this is not self-improvement.
This is resurrection.

Not behavior management.
Heart transformation.

Not “trying harder.”
Being made new.

That means the life God is building in you
is not about proving your worth…

It’s flowing from a worth
that was already secured in Jesus.
“For by grace you have been saved through faith… not a result of works, so that no one may boast.” — Ephesians 2:8–9
Catch this:

You are not working for salvation.
You are walking from salvation.
That changes everything.
But here’s the tension again…
If you’re honest, some of what God is building hurts.
Because He’s not just adding things.
He’s removing things.

Pride.
Hidden sin.
Wrong desires.
Old identities.

And yes… even relationships
that cannot go where He’s taking you.
“Every branch in Me that does not bear fruit He takes away, and every branch that does bear fruit He prunes, that it may bear more fruit.” — John 15:2
Pruning is painful.
But it’s proof you belong to Him.
And this is where grace walks in.

Not soft grace.
Not cheap grace.
Transforming grace.

The kind that meets you in your mess
but refuses to leave you there.

The kind that looks at your worst chapter
and says, “I’m not done writing.”

The kind that takes a sinner
and makes him a son.
So if you’re in a season where:

You feel unseen…
Uncertain…
Unfinished…
Good.
Not because pain is good.
But because God is not finished.
“And we know that for those who love God all things work together for good, for those who are called according to His purpose.” — Romans 8:28
All things.

Not just the wins.
Not just the breakthroughs.

Even the confusion.
Even the waiting.
Even the nights you questioned everything.
God wastes nothing.
So don’t rush the process.

Don’t compare your construction site
to someone else’s highlight reel.
Don’t quit five minutes before breakthrough.
Stay under the hand.

Stay surrendered.
Stay teachable.
Stay close to Jesus.

Because the greatest miracle is not
what God will do through you.
It’s who He is making you to be.
And one day…

What felt like breaking
will be revealed as building.

What felt like loss
will be seen as alignment.

What felt like silence
will echo with purpose.
Jesus is still writing your story.

And grace
is still building your life.
